about: tools/workflows/recipes: rebuilt on the notice tables (devices, notices) that every notice workflow renders. Replaces the reads of tools/tell-the-person, which read through the retired records door. The device's own registration writes its devices row (the app lane); this recipe only reads it, and it writes nothing.

payload.label: Read the notices ready for one of my devices
payload.job: Read the notices addressed to one registered device of the person (or to every device), oldest first after its cursor, with the cursor the device should keep next.
payload.produces: The next notices for one registered device, oldest first, and the cursor to keep, read from the person's own database.

source.from: tools/tell-the-person read-data/told.mjs (myDeviceNotices) and tool:my-device-notices, read on the Workshop's origin/main 75fa3807fc, then rebuilt on devices and notices
source.note: A notice counts for a device when it is addressed to that device or to every device (device_id null), and was made at or after the device registered, so a new registration never receives older notices. The device keeps its cursor; the workflow answers it and writes nothing.

database.description: The name of the person's own database, the one the workflow's tables live in (the store the account keeps its rows in).

after.description: The cursor the device kept: only notices with a number above it (default 0)

steps.title: Make the notice tables if they are absent
steps.do: Run the statements of this step's sql, in order, through tool:run-sql-in-my-database with database = input.database. They only create what is missing, so a run where both tables exist changes nothing. Submit {rendered: true}.

sql.name: devices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (id text PRIMARY KEY, platform text NOT NULL CHECK (platform IN ('live', 'web-push', 'apns')), token text, app_build text, registered_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), last_seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())

sql.name: notices
sql.text: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notices (id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, device_id text REFERENCES devices (id), title text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', body text NOT NULL DEFAULT '', url text, made_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), read_at timestamptz, acted_at timestamptz)

steps.title: Answer the notices ready for this device
steps.do: Trim input.device_id; it is the device's id. Run the statement named device with params [device id]. When it returns no row, or its platform is not live, web-push or apns, refuse with "This device is not registered to read notices.". The platform column is the device's delivery route. The cursor input.after is a whole number from 0 (default 0); the limit input.limit is a whole number from 1 to 100 (default 20). Run the statement named notices with params [device id, after, limit]. Its rows are the notices, oldest first. Answer each one as {id: "told:<id>", title, body, open: url (or null when none), at: made_at as an ISO time, read: true only when read_at is not null}. The cursor: run the statement named last with params [after]. When the notices statement returned fewer rows than limit, the cursor is its last_id; when it returned limit rows, the cursor is the id of the last row returned. Answer {device_id, route: the platform, cursor, notices, said}, where said is "1 notice is ready for this device, oldest first." when there is one notice and "<n> notices are ready for this device, oldest first." otherwise. Nothing is written.

sql.name: device
sql.text: SELECT id, platform FROM devices WHERE id = $1

sql.name: notices
sql.text: SELECT n.id, n.title, n.body, n.url, n.made_at, n.read_at FROM notices n JOIN devices d ON d.id = $1 WHERE n.id > $2::bigint AND (n.device_id = d.id OR n.device_id IS NULL) AND n.made_at >= d.registered_at ORDER BY n.id LIMIT $3

sql.name: last
sql.text: SELECT greatest(coalesce(max(id), 0), $1::bigint) AS last_id FROM notices
